projects.name: Glide
projects.description: Glide is a fast and efficient image loading library for Android focused on smooth scrolling.

queries.prompt_text: What are the main packages (modules) in the Glide library, and what is each one responsible for?
How is the `com.bumptech.glide.load.engine` package structured? What are the key classes and how do they relate to each other?
What is the role of the `Engine` class, and what are its direct dependencies?
must_cover: Engine is the central orchestrator of Glide's image-loading pipeline (manages resource loading and lifecycle).
Mentions a multi-tier cache resolution: at least 3 of {ActiveResources, MemoryCache, in-progress job dedup, new EngineJob+DecodeJob}.
Lists at least 3 of 7 direct dependencies from: MemoryCache, ActiveResources, EngineKeyFactory, Jobs, EngineJobFactory, DecodeJobFactory, LazyDiskCacheProvider.
Mentions at least 2 of 3 listener interfaces Engine implements: EngineJobListener, MemoryCache.ResourceRemovedListener, EngineResource.ResourceListener.

queries.prompt_text: Trace the complete image loading pipeline: what happens from the moment `Glide.with(context).load(url).into(imageView)` is called until the image is displayed? Which classes and methods are involved?
How does the `DecodeJob` interact with `DataFetcherGenerator` and `DecodePath`? Describe the data flow between these components.
What is the class hierarchy of `Target` in Glide? List the inheritance chain and explain the purpose of each level.
must_cover: Identifies Target<R> as the root interface and describes its general role (contract for receiving loaded resources + lifecycle callbacks).
Mentions BaseTarget OR one of its modern alternatives (CustomTarget / CustomViewTarget) as the main abstract base layer.
Names at least 2 intermediate classes with parent links: SimpleTarget, ViewTarget, ImageViewTarget (ImageViewTarget extends ViewTarget).

Names at least 2 concrete leaf classes correctly placed under their parent: e.g., BitmapImageViewTarget / DrawableImageViewTarget under ImageViewTarget; AppWidgetTarget / NotificationTarget / PreloadTarget under CustomTarget.
Briefly explains the purpose of each level mentioned (not just listing names).

queries.prompt_text: What components depend on `DiskCacheStrategy`? How does changing the caching strategy propagate through the system?
must_cover: Identifies DiskCacheStrategy as an abstract class with built-in static constants; names at least 3 of {ALL, NONE, DATA, RESOURCE, AUTOMATIC}.
Mentions the user-facing setter path: RequestBuilder.diskCacheStrategy(...) / BaseRequestOptions stores the field.
Describes the propagation through Engine and DecodeJob (Engine.load → DecodeJob, which consults DiskCacheStrategy to decide cache lookup / writeback).
Explains behavioral impact for at least 2 strategies (e.g., NONE skips disk caching entirely; ALL caches both raw data and transformed resource; RESOURCE caches only post-decode).

queries.prompt_text: How does Glide handle lifecycle management to prevent memory leaks? Which classes are involved in tying image requests to Android Activity/Fragment lifecycles?
Analyze the relationship between `RequestBuilder`, `BaseRequestOptions`, and `RequestOptions`. Is there evidence of the Builder pattern, and how is it structured?
Starting from the `GifDrawable` class, trace all its dependencies up to 3 hops. What subsystems of Glide does GIF support touch?
must_cover: Hop 1: names at least 2 direct dependencies of GifDrawable from {GifFrameLoader, GifDecoder, GifState, Transformation<Bitmap>, BitmapPool, Glide}.
Hop 2: names at least 2 dependencies of GifFrameLoader from {RequestManager, RequestBuilder<Bitmap>, CustomTarget/DelayTarget, RequestOptions, Handler/Looper, BitmapPool, Key/ObjectKey}.
Hop 3: reaches the Glide singleton / GlideContext / Engine layer (notes Engine orchestrates per-frame Bitmap loads).

Categorizes touched subsystems — at least 3 of: decode pipeline, bitmap pool / memory, transformations, request management / lifecycle, resource transcoding, executors / threading, parent-frame loading.

projects.name: DayTrader7
projects.description: DayTrader is a Java EE 7 sample application that simulates an online stock-trading system (originally an IBM WebSphere benchmark). It has a layered architecture: web servlets/JSF -> business EJBs -> JPA entities, with a parallel direct-JDBC implementation of the same business interface.

queries.prompt_text: What is the role of the `TradeAction` class in DayTrader, and what are its direct dependencies?
What is the class hierarchy of the `TradeServices` interface in DayTrader? List the implementing classes and explain the purpose of each implementation.
What components depend on the `OrderDataBean` entity? How does changing the order data structure propagate through the system?
Starting from the `TradeAppServlet` class, trace all its dependencies up to 3 hops. What subsystems of DayTrader does the user-facing servlet touch?
